title: Growth in linear groups
source_version: arXiv:2107.06674v3, 26 April 2024; author manuscript, not independently verified journal typesetting
summary: A dimension obstruction refutes the prime-field bounded-chain theorem used in the diameter proof; an independent rank-one example contradicts the main step bound. Two identity-related auxiliary defects have local repairs. No counterexample to the diameter conclusion or the n>=2 main structure theorem is established.

Local repairs do not certify a complete revised diameter or main structural proof.

problems.assumptions: n=4, p>=5 prime, q=p², P=M2(F_q)^+ in upper block, L=SL2(q)xSL2(q) diagonal, G=P semidirect L. G finite; O_p(G)=P; P normalized; deg_C(G)>=(q-1)/2 unbounded.
problems.check: All left/right M2(F_q) multiplication preserves any invariant F_p subspace, so P is irreducible dimension8. Both quasisimple factors act nontrivially. Any nontrivial F_p representation of SL2(q) has dimension>=3 by root-group kernel and squares span argument. Required tensor has dimension>=9.
problems.result: No B-bounded invariant chain exists. The actual diameter-proof section [G,Sol(G)]/its derived subgroup is exactly P.
problems.counterevidence: Natural tensor product over F_q exists; no failure of algebraically closed tensor decomposition and no final-diameter counterexample. No finite quasirandom threshold fixes the F_p obstruction.
problems.impact: False structural theorem is applied to exact counterexample family in the core diameter proof.
problems.correction: No full correction verified. Need compatible field descent/constituents and orbit-growth induction; changing only the tensor subscript is insufficient.

checks.source_anchors: author v3 Definition 9.4, Theorem 9.6 and Lemma 9.7, PDF pp34-36; main.tex2171-2330
checks.reason: For q=p^2,p>=5, P=M_2(F_q)^+ has F_p-dimension 8 and is irreducible under SL_2(q)xSL_2(q): elementary unipotents span both matrix algebras. It cannot be a tensor product of nontrivial F_p representations of both factors, since each such factor has dimension >=3. A hypothetical 2-dimensional representation kills a nonzero element of U=C_p^2, diagonal conjugation kills all U, hence SL_2(q). The semidirect group is a fixed-rank GL_4 example with arbitrarily large complex representation degree: nonzero U-character torus orbits have size (q-1)/2, and a representation killing the Levi factors also kills [P,L]=P. Thus no hidden small-quasirandomness or module-filtration exception removes the witness. Theorem 9.6's field-descent tensor premise is false and is used on P/[P,P] in the diameter proof.
checks.counterevidence: This disproves a structural input and the supplied proof route, not the final diameter estimate. Lemma 9.7's X+X cyclic-submodule inference and the quotient-generator-lift commutator inference are independently invalid; neither is automatically a counterexample to its ultimate bound.
checks.repair_check: An actual replacement for the F_p tensor assertion and the lifting argument is required; scalar-extension notation alone does not descend the tensor factors.

checks.counterevidence: The example concerns the admitted rank-one endpoint; it does not refute n>=2.
checks.repair_check: Restrict to n>=2 or use max(1,n-1). For rank one, Gamma=<A>,H=1 provides the abelian repair.

checks.reason: The source defines symmetry only by inverse closure and A^k as exactly k factors. V=C_2,G=1,d=1,A={v},K=2 meets all hypotheses including deg_C(1)=infinity; A^7={v} excludes [V,G]={0}. The proof incorrectly uses g in B although only G subset B^2 is automatic.

checks.reason: In F_p semidirect {+1,-1}, A consists of three reflections x->-x+b,b=-1,0,1. It is symmetric and 3-tripling, projects to {-1}, generates T, and satisfies the section fixed-point hypotheses. All root images of A have size1, so alternative (a) fails. A^2 contains a nonzero translation, generating V, while no fixed exact odd power contains translations and any fixed even power has at most 2m+1 translations for p sufficiently large. Thus alternative (b) also fails as stated.
checks.counterevidence: The downstream use already includes the identity, so the standalone counterexample does not refute that application.
checks.repair_check: Add 1 in A (or explicitly switch to padded powers); this restores the initial root-size dichotomy and the pivoting use.

additional_scope_checks: The p31 T-span correction is supported with J=((U1 intersect H2)H2')/H2' <= V, not an unspecified image of all U1. T-stability and coprime action give L_T=[L_T,T] <= image[U1 intersect H2,T] <= trace([U1,T],V).
The p21 projection-to-trace/intersection passage remains Needs Evidence: projection onto a quotient does not alone prove intersection coverage. No new decisive counterexample was established.
Characteristic endpoint, finite normal-generation and high-rank objections were assessed with the report's existing limits; imported finite-group and mixing theorems were not re-proved.
